chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from a man, all from Zurara, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: 'What do you say about the People of the A'raf?' I said: 'They are nothing but either believers or disbelievers. If they enter Paradise, they are believers, and if they enter the Fire, they are disbelievers.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'By Allah, they are neither believers nor disbelievers. Had they been believers, they would have entered Paradise just as the believers entered it, and had they been disbelievers, they would have entered the Fire just as the disbelievers entered it. But they are a people whose good deeds and evil deeds are equal, so their deeds fell short, and indeed they are as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said.'

I said: 'Are they from the people of Paradise or from the people of the Fire?' He said: 'Leave them where Allah has left them.' I said: 'So shall I postpone them?' He said: 'Yes, I postpone them just as Allah has postponed them. If He wills, He will admit them to Paradise by His mercy, and if He wills, He will drive them to the Fire because of their sins, and He will not wrong them.'

I said: 'Will a disbeliever enter Paradise?' He said: 'No.' I said: 'Will anyone enter the Fire except a disbeliever?' He said: 'No, except if Allah wills. O Zurara! Indeed, I say 'What Allah wills', and you do not say 'What Allah wills'. Know that when you grow old, you will retract, and your knots will be loosened from you.'
ai.seo_question: Who are the People of the A'raf and what is their fate according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (AS) elucidates the status of the People of the Heights (Ashab al-A'raf) as a distinct intermediate group whose good and evil deeds are perfectly balanced, preventing immediate entry into either Paradise or Hell. The Imam emphasizes their state of 'suspension' (tarjih), where their ultimate fate remains contingent upon Allah's will—either through divine mercy or the weight of their sins—highlighting the balance between justice and grace in Shia eschatology. This discussion underscores the concept of purgatorial waiting, where the barrier of the Heights serves as a temporary abode for those awaiting final judgment.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from a man, altogether from Zurara who said,

‘Abu Ja’farasws said to me: ‘What you saying regarding [7:48] the people of Al-Araf?’ So I said, ‘They are not except either Momineen or Kafireen (unbelievers). If they enter the Paradise, so they are Momineen, and if they enter the Fire, so they are Kafireen (unbelievers).

So heasws said: ‘By Allahazwj! They are neither Momineen nor Kafireen (unbelievers), and had they been Momineen they would have entered the Paradise just as the Momineen would enter it, and had they been Kafireen (unbelievers) they would have entered the Fire just as the Kafireen (unbelievers) would enter. But, they are a people whose good and evil deeds are equal, so the deeds are deficient with them, and they are just as Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Says’.

So I said, ‘Are they from the inhabitants of the Paradise or from the inhabitants of the Fire?’ So he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘Leave them where Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> has left them’. I said, ‘So shall I postpone them?’ He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, postpone them just as Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> has Postponed them. If He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> so Desires to He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> would Enter them into the Paradise by His<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mercy, and if He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> so Desires to He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> would Usher them to the Fire due to their sins, and He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> would not be unjust to them’.

So I said, ‘Would a Kafir (unbeliever) enter the Paradise?’ Heasws said: ‘No’. I said, ‘Would anyone enter the Fire except for a Kafir (unbeliever)?’ So heasws said: ‘No. except if Allahazwj so Desires. O Zurara! Iasws am saying: ‘Whatever Allahazwj so Desires’, and you are not saying, ‘Whatever Allahazwj so Desires’. But, you, when you get older, would retract, and your knots would be loosened from you’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr and Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from a man all from Zurara who has said the following:

“Once, abu Ja’far (a.s.) asked me, ‘What do you say about the people of al-‘A’raf?’ I said, ‘They are either believing people or unbelievers. If they will enter paradise they will be believing people, and if they go in fire they will be unbelievers.’

The Imam then said, ‘By Allah, they are not believing people nor are they unbelievers. Had they been of the believers they would have entered paradise like the believers. Were they unbelievers they would have gone in fire like the unbelievers. They, however, are a people whose good and bad deeds are equal. Their deeds fall short and they are as Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has said they are.’

I asked, ‘Are they among the people of paradise or of the people of fire?’ The Imam said, ‘Leave them as Allah has done.’ I said, ‘Do you leave them in postponement?’ The Imam said, ‘Yes, just as Allah has done. If He will wish. He will send them in paradise through His favor, and if He will wish He will drive them to fire for their sins; He will not be doing injustice to them.’

I asked, ‘Will unbelievers enter paradise?’ The Imam said, ‘No.’ I said, ‘Will anyone besides unbelievers go to fire?’ The Imam said, ‘No, unless Allah will wish. O Zurara, I say, ‘As Allah wills and you do not say, ‘As Allah wills.’ When you will grow up you will turn back and your knots ease up (on your opponent).”’
